title: NDPS cases involving juvenile accused - special considerations
p1:
A teenager caught with drugs is not always treated the same way as an adult accused under the law.

Many people assume that an NDPS case automatically means the same punishment applies to everyone involved. But when the accused is a child, the legal approach changes significantly.
p2:
A surprising aspect is that juvenile justice focuses not only on the alleged offence, but also on the child's age, circumstances, background, and chances of rehabilitation.

Even in serious cases under the NDPS Act, authorities must consider special procedures meant for children in conflict with law.
p3:
The key difference is that the system aims to balance accountability with reform. A juvenile accused may have different protections, procedures, and rehabilitation-focused measures compared with an adult accused.

This distinction matters because a child's future cannot be viewed only through the lens of one incident. Early legal guidance and proper representation can influence the outcome significantly.
conclusion: Should juvenile NDPS cases focus more on punishment or rehabilitation, considering the long-term impact on a child's future?
